label: EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 — Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA)
body: 1. Know your transfers. Map all flows of personal data — origin, destination, importer, data categories, purpose. Apply to onward transfers too.
2. Identify the Article 46 transfer tool. SCCs, BCRs, code of conduct, certification, or Art. 49 derogation if exceptional.

3. Assess the third-country law and practice. Public-authority access regime, surveillance laws (FISA §702, EO 12333, equivalents), redress mechanisms, rule of law indicators. EDPB references on essential guarantees (WP237 + supplementary).

4. Identify and adopt supplementary measures if step 3 reveals gaps. Three categories: (a) technical — strong encryption with EU-held keys, split-key pseudonymisation, EU-hosted intermediaries; (b) contractual — Schrems II-aligned commitments, transparency on requests, audit rights; (c) organisational — internal policies, training, dedicated personnel, transparency reports.
5. Procedural steps. Where supplementary measures address the gaps, proceed with the transfer; otherwise, suspend the transfer.
6. Re-evaluate at appropriate intervals. When law in the third country changes, or when scope of transfers expands.
Annex 2 lists encryption and pseudonymisation use-cases the EDPB has explicitly accepted; Use Cases 6 + 7 (cloud service provider with US importer holding keys) remain rejected.
